rows.event: Contemporary report of announced PC-communication service
rows.evidence_status: announced service date in contemporary report; actual opening not independently established
rows.date_tooltip: Nexon’s October 17 presentation reportedly announced PC-communication service for October 18, 1997; the contemporary article calls it commercial service, while later sources distinguish a January 1998 formal opening. No client number is known.
rows.recommendation: Eligible as an explicitly qualified announced-date milestone, not a confirmed open-beta row or numbered release
limitations: Article publication date and announced date are both October 18; this is not a Wayback-date inference.
Article calls the planned service commercial, conflicting with later formal-opening chronology; do not relabel it open beta without stronger evidence.
Korean service context is supported; the earlier English Kingdom of the Winds announcement must not be reassigned to U.S. Dark Ages.

rows.date_tooltip: NEXON Korea’s official 10,000-day notice explicitly dates formal Legend of Darkness service opening to January 3, 1998. It does not identify the client version.
rows.recommendation: Add as confirmed service milestone with unknown client version
limitations: Retrospective 2025 publisher statement; not a recovered 1998 installer.
The publisher says formal service, not a numeric client release.

rows.event: Reported U.S. Dark Ages release date
rows.evidence_status: editorial/community database date; original publisher launch-day notice not recovered
rows.date_tooltip: RPGFan explicitly lists August 2, 1999 for the U.S. Dark Ages edition; MobyGames also lists this date. No original publisher launch announcement or client number has been established.
rows.recommendation: Use only an evidence-labeled reported-date placeholder if the catalog admits such milestones; omit from a publisher-confirmed-only date set
limitations: This is U.S. Dark Ages evidence, not a second Korean launch.
RPGFan labels the overall entry Dark Ages Medenia, so do not confuse the 1999 base-game date with the 2003 expansion.
MobyGames entry initially added by David Kennerly but current field has later contributors; this is not independently verified director authorship of that field.

GameMeca repeats August 2, 1999 in Korean-title database metadata while its NDC report discusses January 1998 commercialization; this mixed-region/conflicting field is not independent Korean launch evidence.
Mirrored official Candle News16 is dated August 2, 1999 but only reports connectivity; it does not announce launch.
